messages:
maria: FYI — customer acme-corp seeing intermittent 503/500 from hosted inference since 04:36 UTC. They report latency spikes and some requests return 'upstream worker closed connection'. Ticket #12345 opened.

infra-bot: [alert] 04:36:12 UTC - infer-worker-restart spike on pool-hosted-us-west (20 restarts in 5m) :rotating_light:

oncall-bot: paging oncall (kai) for incident escalation.

kai: Oncall here. Can we get a short reproduction and which model/route is failing? Any recent deploys?

maria: Model: open-13b-1, route: /v1/generate (hosted-prod-us-west). No user deploys pushed in the last hour from the app side. Customer load ~120 qps, burst to 400 qps. Sample curl returns 503 with body 'upstream worker exited' and trace header x-upstream-exit=1. Logs attached below.

maria: ```
2026-03-16T04:36:12Z runner[4521]: runtime error: invalid memory address 
2026-03-16T04:36:12Z infer-worker[4521]: segfault at 0 ip=0x7f... sp=0x7ffd...
2026-03-16T04:36:12Z gpu-monitor: GPU0 OOM while allocating 1.2GiB for attention_kv_cache
2026-03-16T04:36:12Z kernel: container(4521) killed with signal 11
```

raj: That looks like a mixed OOM + segfault. Any sign of a kernel or driver update on the nodes?

kai: Not on the node images. We did roll an autoscaler policy yesterday that reduces spare capacity faster. Could be memory pressure from larger batches + kv prefetch.

emma: We also enabled a change to continuous batching thresholds (lower latency targets) in the runtime 3 days ago. If batch sizes increased, kv cache usage jumps and can cause OOMs for some model variants.

maria: Customer says failures started roughly when their QPS spiked and coincides with our autoscaler churn. I'm running a quick repro with a synthetic load at 350 qps to the same model route.

support-bot: Impact: acme-corp (acct 9983) - P1, degraded for 18 minutes, multiple customers affected, billing unaffected but SLA hit possible.

oncall-bot: Runbook snippet: 1) Pin traffic to fallback model variant (smaller KV footprint) 2) Temporarily scale up reserved capacity for pool-hosted-us-west 3) Roll back batching threshold change if repro confirmed 4) Collect core dumps + GPU driver logs and attach to ticket.

maria: Actioned step 1: pinned routing to model-13b-compact-v1 for acme-corp and injected a temporary per-account concurrency cap (50). Also initiated rolling restart of 4 affected worker instances with previous runtime build.

kai: Good. Please collect: `dmesg` around the crash, `nvidia-smi -q` before/after, container stdout/stderr, and core dump (if available). Also run `gpu_top` to check per-process VRAM usage.

maria: Uploading logs to ticket now. Quick note from repro: when synthetic load hit sustained 380 qps with batch target=64 we reproduced a deterministic GPU OOM and the worker process segfaulted. Lowering batch target to 16 prevented the crash.

raj: That strongly points at batching change interacting with kv prefetch memory growth. Can we rollback the batching thresholds in runtime config and roll nodes forward slowly?

emma: I'll submit a rollback to runtime config (revert continuous-batching spike) and start canary in us-west with reduced batch target.

maria: Customer routed to fallback model, error rate dropped to 0.8% from 12% in 12m. They're on the call and appreciate quick mitigation.

kai: Next steps: 1) collect full core + GPU logs (emma/raj) 2) telemetry: add a per-model kv-cache memory metric (infra) 3) longer-term: runtime must clamp batch targets when expected GPU mem per-seq exceeds threshold.

raj: I'll take the telemetry work after the rollback.

oncall-bot: Incident severity: P1 -> P2 after mitigation. Continue monitoring for 2 hours, then re-evaluate.

maria: Thanks all — will update the ticket with logs and customer note.

kai: Thanks. I'll follow up with a short RCA doc tomorrow after we analyze core and batch interactions.
